_note: Physics-based pools on the art grid (src/vfx/splat_shape.gd shape, src/vfx/pool_paint.gd drawing). A pool runs out from where it lands along its flight; walls and solid props stop it and its volume runs on along them (a corner fills, the open floor gets a stretched blot). squash = how flat it lies (the floor seen at a slant); momentum 0..1 = how far it keeps sliding along its flight; spread_time = s it takes to run out to its rim; edge_time = s its rim goes before its middle at the end; rebake_hz = how often a changing pool is shaded again at most; anim_hz = the frame rate of living materials (fire, lava); bake_budget_ms = ms per frame for working out and shading the fields again, in slices (the one waiting longest first, a new one at once; the last picture shows until the new one is done), so their costs do not pile up in one frame; lay_budget_ms = ms per frame for laying a pool into a field that holds cells already (from its middle out, far ahead of its spreading; on empty floor it goes in at once), lay_now_cells = a pool of at most this many cells is laid at once; catch_up_after_ms / catch_up_ms = a picture or pool waiting longer than this gets this many ms a frame instead of the budget above (a huge field does not lag far behind, the frames stay bounded); thread_cells = a pool of this many cells or more gets its shape worked out on a worker thread (it shows a few frames later, the game never waits for it). materials: style (liquid, void, ice, fire, lava), droplets = drops a thrown splat flings ahead, bubbles = bubbles at a time, splash = what a landing pool throws (drops, chips, embers, none), ripple = speed of its rings (0 none), steps = wet steps behind waders, ramp = opaque colours by role (spec specular, hi highlight and north rim, lite light swirls, body, shade, deep south row and lip, outline). Materials are opaque (no alpha); see production/qa/evidence/crypt-vfx-review. void_pull = [pull, spin] px/s of a void pool's well (it pulls loose things in), void_motes = streaks circling in per second.

physics._note: The living liquid (src/vfx/pool_paint.gd): a pool first seen within splash_window s of landing throws drops (drops_per_px of its radius, at most drop_max) at drop_speed px/s along its flight with drop_lift px/s upwards; a drop into its pool rings it, next to it joins it, on dry floor lies as a puddle for drop_dry s (drawing only). Rings run at ripple_speed art px/s (times the material's ripple) for ripple_life s (at most ripple_max per material), a crown jumps for crown_time s. Waders ring every wade_every s; out of a liquid with steps they leave steps wet steps, one per stride crypt px, that dry in step_dry s. User request 2026-10-30: liquids as physics. Burning ground lets fire_flames flames per cell and second rise (at most fire_flames_max per pool layer material). Materials: spread_scale slows the run-out (lava is thick: 3), glow = strength of the warm light breathing over the pool. Ice (materials crack, melt_to): a blow cracks it (at most crack_max cracks, healing over crack_life s), a frost burst freezes liquid rim first over freeze_time s, ice that goes leaves melt water drying in water_dry s. Lightning into a liquid (electrify): arcs crawl over it for zap_time s in zap_cols. A puddle the game charged (src/combat/boss_moves.gd electrify, balance.json element; user request 2026-10-30: water and lightning make a puddle that works) crackles all over while charged: zap_charged_arcs arcs per 100 cells, zap_charged_len cells each, in zap_charged_cols.

reactions._note: Where two materials meet (keyed <style>+<style>; liquid = poison, blood, water): a_to / b_to say what becomes of each cell there: gone (hidden; drawing only, the game's hit test is untouched), crust (lava turns dark for crust_time s and glows up again), or a material name (a drawing-only cell of it); steam hisses every steam_every cells. A liquid on the hot floor (the Hell's lava tiles) reacts as liquid+lava. User decision 2026-10-30: reactions visible only.
